title: CoT Faithfulness Variation by Task Type: Math vs. Factual vs. Ethical vs. Commonsense
original_idea: Replicate the Anthropic CoT faithfulness methodology (hint injection, post-hoc rationalization detection) across four task types. Measure unfaithfulness rate by category.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding which task types have more unfaithful CoT directly informs where safety monitoring should be concentrated. Actionable for deployment decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Hint injection methodology requires careful experimental design. Four task types multiply the work. Moderately accessible but requires understanding of the methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four task types each requiring scenario design, data collection, and analysis is too broad for 30hrs. Would need to reduce to 2 task types to be feasible.

title: Sycophancy Stress Test Using Fictitious User Profiles
original_idea: Prefix identical false-premise questions with different user identity framings (novice user, domain expert, emotionally distressed user, skeptical peer) and measure capitulation rates across profile types.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly relevant to personalized AI safety. If models are more sycophantic to certain profiles, that is actionable for deployment guardrails.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Very straightforward experiment design: prefix variations on the same questions. API calls and counting. Highly accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 4 user profiles x a set of questions is manageable. Could focus on 1-2 models and 20-30 questions. Well-scoped for 30hrs.

title: Does Fine-Tuning GPT-5 for CoT Controllability Improve Faithfulness?
original_idea: Use the open GPT-5 API with system-prompt-level fine-tuning signals (if accessible) or use a controllable open-source equivalent. Fine-tune on a small dataset of (scenario, desired CoT behavior) pairs. Measure faithfulness before and after.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding whether controllability fine-tuning helps faithfulness is directly safety-relevant and could change how models are trained.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning requires significant ML expertise, dataset curation, and compute management. GPT-5 fine-tuning API access and cost are barriers. Not beginner-appropriate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Fine-tuning, dataset creation, pre/post evaluation, and analysis is extensive. Would likely exceed 30hrs significantly.

title: Is GPT-5's Low CoT Controllability Consistent Across Model Sizes?
original_idea: Measure CoT controllability using OpenAI's forbidden-word methodology on GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, and GPT-5, and replicate with Llama 3.1 at multiple sizes. Plot controllability vs. scale.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding the relationship between scale and controllability is fundamental to scaling safety. Direct policy implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Forbidden-word methodology is straightforward but running Llama at multiple sizes requires local GPU setup. API models are easier. Mixed accessibility.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Testing across 6+ model sizes/families is broad. Running Llama locally at large scales needs significant compute time. Hard to complete in 30hrs.

title: Can In-Context Honesty Instructions Rescue Sycophancy Under Pressure for Claude Opus 4.5?
original_idea: Run the Claude Opus 4.5 sycophancy correction experiment with and without explicit honesty-enabling system prompts. Measure whether course-correction rate improves and whether it degrades other behavior.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests an immediately deployable intervention against a documented safety failure. High impact if prompt engineering works; important negative result if it doesn't.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: API calls with different system prompts. Counting correction rates. Very straightforward for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single model, single documented failure, with/without prompt variants. Very well-scoped. Could add a few prompt variants within 30hrs.

title: Does System Prompt Framing Affect Sycophancy Recovery Across Model Families?
original_idea: Run identical multi-turn sycophancy correction scenarios on Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Llama 3.1 70B, with and without honesty-enabling system prompts. Compare baseline and prompted correction rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cross-model comparison of a safety intervention is valuable for understanding whether the problem is industry-wide.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: API calls across multiple providers. Straightforward methodology. Slightly more complex than single-model due to multiple APIs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four model families with multi-turn scenarios is broad. API costs and setup for 4 providers plus analysis. Hard to do well in 30hrs.

title: Is Low CoT Controllability Replicated in Chain-of-Draft or Compressed Reasoning Models?
original_idea: Apply the forbidden-word or hint-injection controllability test to models with different CoT lengths (standard, compressed, minimal scratchpad). Measure whether controllability correlates with CoT verbosity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting for understanding CoT controllability but the practical safety implications depend on whether compressed CoT models become widely deployed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires access to chain-of-draft models and compressed reasoning variants, which are less readily available. Configuring different CoT modes adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: If limited to 2-3 models with different CoT modes, could be feasible. But finding and setting up compressed-CoT variants adds overhead.

title: Replicating TruthfulQA Inverse Scaling on Newer Model Generations
original_idea: Run TruthfulQA across all accessible sizes in the Llama 3.1, Gemma 2, and Qwen 2.5 families. Plot truthfulness score vs. parameter count. Test whether inverse scaling persists.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Inverse scaling is a fundamental safety concern. Confirming or refuting it on current models has direct implications for scaling policy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TruthfulQA is a standard benchmark with existing tooling. But running multiple model sizes locally requires GPU management experience.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three model families at multiple sizes each is extensive. Even with existing benchmarks, running and analyzing all combinations exceeds 30hrs.

title: Replicating Sycophancy Results in Non-English Languages
original_idea: Translate a subset of ELEPHANT or TRUTH DECAY scenarios into Spanish, Mandarin, and Arabic. Run across the same model families and compare sycophancy rates across languages.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Language-dependent sycophancy is a real equity and safety concern for global AI deployment. High impact if disparities are found.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Translation requires language expertise or quality verification. Running experiments is straightforward but validating non-English results adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three languages x multiple models x translation validation is broad. Could narrow to Spanish only for a BAISH team, but still substantial.

title: Replicating CoT Faithfulness Results on Open-Source Models with White-Box Access
original_idea: Replicate the hint-injection unfaithfulness paradigm on Llama 3.1 8B with white-box access. Use activation patching to verify whether the hint representation is active during answer generation even when absent from CoT.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Mechanistic evidence for CoT unfaithfulness is a high-value safety contribution. Goes beyond behavioral proxies to provide causal evidence.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Activation patching requires deep mechanistic interpretability expertise. Understanding transformer internals, implementing patching, and interpreting results is advanced.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Setting up white-box access, implementing activation patching, running experiments, and analyzing results. Well beyond 30hrs for beginners.

title: Replicating Sycophancy Benchmarks in Code Debugging Scenarios
original_idea: Create a benchmark of buggy code snippets paired with user insistence framings ('This code works correctly, right?'). Measure rate at which models falsely validate buggy code vs. correctly flag the bug.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Code review sycophancy is directly safety-relevant for developer tools. Practical impact on how AI coding assistants are deployed and trusted.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: CS students are ideal for this: they can write buggy code, understand bugs, and evaluate model responses. API calls with prompts. Very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Creating 30-50 buggy code snippets with pressure framings and testing 1-2 models is well within 30hrs. Clear deliverable.

title: Replicating ELEPHANT Social Sycophancy on Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models
original_idea: Run ELEPHANT scenarios on base (non-instruction-tuned) and instruction-tuned variants of the same models. Compare social sycophancy rates to isolate the contribution of instruction tuning.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Isolating whether sycophancy comes from pre-training vs instruction tuning directly informs mitigation strategy. High diagnostic value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running base models requires understanding of completion-style prompting (different from chat). ELEPHANT benchmark setup adds moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Could focus on one model family (e.g., Llama base vs instruct) with a subset of ELEPHANT. Feasible if well-scoped but requires careful setup.

title: A Minimal Realistic Sycophancy Benchmark from Naturalistic Conversation Data
original_idea: Extract 200-400 naturalistic false-premise exchanges from LMSYS-Chat-1M or WildChat. Label model responses for sycophancy (agrees with false premise, hedges, or corrects). Release a small but ecologically valid benchmark dataset.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A naturalistic benchmark fills a recognized gap and enables validation of synthetic benchmarks. High community value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Data filtering and labeling are straightforward tasks. Downloading and processing large datasets requires some data engineering but is manageable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Filtering through millions of conversations to find 200-400 relevant exchanges, then labeling them, is moderate scope. Could be tight for 30hrs but feasible with good filtering.

title: A Lightweight CoT Faithfulness Benchmark Using Hint Injection
original_idea: Build a 100-item benchmark using the hint-injection paradigm: provide a model with a scenario that contains a hidden hint favoring the correct answer, then check whether the CoT mentions the hint and whether the answer is consistent with it. Release code and data.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Standardized benchmarks are infrastructure for the field. A lightweight CoT faithfulness benchmark enables cross-study comparison.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing hint-injection scenarios and coding an evaluation pipeline is accessible for CS students. Clear methodology from existing papers.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 items with a clear paradigm is well-scoped. Design, implement, validate on 1-2 models. Fits within 30hrs.

title: HonestyScope: A Multi-Dimensional Honesty Measurement Suite
original_idea: Design a test suite with separate batteries for: (1) false-premise capitulation, (2) calibration under pressure, (3) lying by omission, and (4) epistemic cowardice. Score models across all four dimensions. Release as open source.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Multi-dimensional honesty measurement addresses a fundamental gap. Captures failure modes that single-metric tools miss.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing 4 separate measurement batteries requires understanding of different honesty failure modes. Operationalizing lying by omission and epistemic cowardice is non-trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four separate batteries, each requiring design, implementation, and validation, is far too broad for 30hrs. This is a multi-month project.
